import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert 'date' column to datetime
coffee_sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'])

# Convert 'is_takeaway' column to categorical
coffee_sales['is_takeaway'] = coffee_sales['is_takeaway'].apply(lambda x: 'Yes' if x == 1 else 'No')

# Melt the data to create a pivoted table
coffee_sales_pivoted = pd.melt(coffee_sales, id_vars=['date', 'payment_method', 'customer_age_group', 'is_takeaway'], 
                               var_name='product', value_name='quantity')

# Create a stacked bar chart for the top 5 products by quantity
top_5_products = coffee_sales_pivoted['product'].value_counts().head(5).index

# Filter the data to only include the top 5 products
top_5_products_data = coffee_sales_pivoted[coffee_sales_pivoted['product'].isin(top_5_products)]

# Create the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.countplot(data=top_5_products_data, x='product', hue='payment_method', ax=plt.gca())
plt.title('Top 5 Products by Quantity')
plt.xlabel('Product')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.legend(title='Payment Method', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.xticks(rotation=90)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
